raw_glosses: (uncountable) The chemical element (symbol Kr) with an atomic number of 36. It is a colourless, odourless noble gas that only reacts with fluorine. It is one of the rarest gases in the Earth's atmosphere.
glosses: The chemical element (symbol Kr) with an atomic number of 36. It is a colourless, odourless noble gas that only reacts with fluorine. It is one of the rarest gases in the Earth's atmosphere.

examples.text: The terrific seven-grain bread here is the kryptonite of restaurant reviewers: two mini-loaves and you are incapacitated.
examples.ref: 1991 October 25, Bryan Miller, “Restaurants: John Clancy's”, in The New York Times, archived from the original on 12 Feb 2021:

examples.text: So while recording or sampling a Charlie Manson track […] makes for shock rock kudos aplenty, a devotion to Hubbard is kryptonite for credibility.
examples.ref: 2006 March 25, Jonathan Leggett, “Cult musicians”, in The Guardian, archived from the original on 26 Feb 2025:

examples.text: We all have our own kryptonite or kryptonites, so don't tempt yourself by listening to so-called friends who are just demonic tools being used to bring you under.
examples.ref: 2016, Marlon Orlando Cole, Orphans: Nature's Beloved, page 93:

examples.text: But of course porn is kryptonite to many investors.
examples.ref: 2025 May 24, “OnlyFans has a shot at ditching its NSFW image”, in FT Weekend (Lex. section), London: The Financial Times Ltd., →ISSN, →OCLC, page 20:

raw_glosses: (figuratively) The one weakness of something or someone that is otherwise invulnerable.
